title: Energy Commission Amendment Bill, 2023
text:
ENERGY COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2023

MEMORANDUM
The object of the Bill is to amend the Energy Commission Act, 1997

(Act 541) to revise upwards the correlative penalties for offences
committed under the Act, to provide for the imposition of administrative
penalties and to empower the Minister responsible for Energy, on the
advice of the Commission, to make Regulations on the unlawful
connection to an equipment, an installation or a facility for the supply,
transmission, distribution or sale of electricity or natural gas, and for the
importation, assembly, manufacture, sale, installation and operation of
equipment and accessories for the transmission, wholesale supply,
distribution or sale of electricity or natural gas, and other related matters.

The Energy Commission Act, 1997 (Act 541) was enacted to establish
the Energy Commission with a mandate to regulate and manage the
development and utilisation of energy resources and grant licences for
the transmission, wholesale supply, distribution and sale of electricity
and natural gas among other related functions.

In 2016 the Act was amended to provide for the promotion of local
content and local participation in the Electricity Supply Industry in
Ghana.

The Commission has for the past twenty-five years played its role as
an effective technical regulator of the electricity and natural gas sectors.
During that period, the Commission has observed several infractions of
the provisions of the Act. The penalties stipulated for the various offences
under section 54 of Act 541 are not deterrent enough to guarantee
compliance with the respective provisions of the Act. In particular, the
failure to obtain a licence to carry out specific activities; the unlawful
destruction or damage of equipment, an installation of a facility for the
supply, transmission, distribution or sale of electricity or natural gas; or
the failure to comply with a standard of performance prescribed by the
Commission attracts a penalty which does not necessarily correlate to
the gravity of the offence. Furthermore, the absence of an upper threshold
does not provide a yardstick to determine the range of penalties that may
be imposed for the different categories of offences.

ENERGY COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2023

The increasing trend of malpractices dealing with unlawful
connections on the part of some consumers and non-consumers in the
electricity supply industry, has sometimes led to overload of the power
distribution systems and consequently resulted in bad voltage quality from
the suppliers. Other issues emanating from connection malpractices have
been the recurrent fire outbreaks oi Jamage to electrical appliances of
other consumers and invariably the loss of revenue to Government and
the utilities that provide power.

The unlawful means of connecting to an electric current source
without the knowledge of licensed distribution utilities have adverse effects
such as contributing to high commercial losses to the licensed utilities
and consequently impacting on the bills of other consumers. Additionally,
this results in unfair competition among businesses, since those who do
not indulge in unlawful connections end up with a higher overhead
expenditure or cost as compared to those who indulge in unlawful
connections.

Act 541 does not address these problems and the Bill seeks to plug
the loopholes by creating an offence and correlative penalty.

The inablity of the Commission to impose adminstrative penalties
is also a basis for the amendment of Act 541. The imposition of
administrative penalties under Act 541 will provide a mechanism for the
Commission to ensure regulatory compliance.

In sync with the creation of the new offence of unlawful connections,
the Bill further provides for the enactment of Regulations in respect of
unlawful connections of electricity and natural gas. The Bill further
empowers the Minister, on the advice of the Commission, to make
Regulations to prohibit the manufacture, importation, assembly, sale and
installation of equipment and accessories except by persons licensed or
registered by the Commission.

Clause 1 of the Bill amends section 41 of the Energy Commission
Act, 1997 (Act 541) to include as part of the sources of funds in the Energy 

ii

ENERGY COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2023

Fund, funds realised by the Commission from the imposition of
administrative penalties.

Clause 2 of the Bill amends in part, subsection (1) of section 54 of
the Energy Commission Act, 1997 (Act 541) to include a new offence of
unlawful connection to an equipment, an installation or a facility for the
supply, transmission, distribution or sale of electricity or natural gas.
The clause further amends subsection (1) of section 54 to revise upwards
the penalty units and the term of imprisonment for an offence committed
under the section.

Clause 3 amends the Act by the introduction of a new section 54A,
on administrative penalties.

Clause 4 amends section 56 of Act 541 to empower the Minister to
make Regulations in respect of unlawful connection to an equipment, an
installation or a facility for the supply, transmission, distribution or sale
of electricity or natural gas and for the importation, assembly,
manufacture, sale, installation and operation of equipment and accessories
for the transmission, wholesale supply, distribution or sale of electricity
or natural gas.

Clause 4 further amends section 56 by the repeal of subsection (2)
which is spent in the light of the repeal of the Statutory Instruments Act
1959 (No. 52) by section 52 of the Interpretation Act, 2009 (Act 792).

Clause 5 amends section 57 on interpretation to define “unlawful
connection”.

Hon. Dr. Matthew Opoku Prempeh
Minister responsible for Energy

Section

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

BILL
ENTITLED

ENERGY COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023

AN ACT to amend the Energy Commission Act, 1997 (Act 541) to
provide for the offence of unlawful connection to an equipment,
an installation or a facility for die supply, transmission, distribution
or sale of electricity or natural gas; to revise upwards the penalties
for offences; to provide for the imposition of administrative
penalties and for related matters.

PASSED by Parliament and assented to by the President:

Section 41 of Act 541 amended
1. The Energy Commission Act, 1997 (Act 541) referred to in this Act

as the principal enactment is amended in subsection (2) of section 41 by
the insertion after paragraph (b), of

“(ba) administrative penalties relating to contraventions
under section 54A.”.

2

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

Section 54 of Act 541 amended
2. The principal enactment is amended by the substitution for

section 54, of

“(1) A person shall not

(a) install or operate a facility for the transmission,
wholesale supply, distribution or sale of
electricity or natural gas without a licence
from the Commission as provided for
under this Act; or

(b) unlawfully destroy or damage an equipment,
an installation or a facility for the supply,
transmission, distribution or sale of
electricity or natural gas; or

(c) unlawfully connect to an equipment, an
installation or a facility for the supply,
transmission, distribution or sale of
electricity or natural gas;

(2) A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits
an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine of
not less than ten thousand penalty units and not more than
twenty thousand penalty units or to a term of imprisonment
of not less than two years and not more than five years or
to both on first conviction, and to a fine of not less than
twenty thousand penalty units and not more than fifty
thousand penalty units or to a term of imprisonment of
not less than five years and not more than seven years or to
both on a subsequent conviction.

(3) Where an offence under this Act or the Regulations,
is committed by a body corporate or by a member of a
partnership or other firm, every director or officer of that 

3

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

body corporate or a member of the partnership or any other
person concerned with the management of the firm shall
be deemed to have committed that offence and is liable on
conviction, to a fine of not less than twenty thousand penalty
units and not more than fifty thousand penalty units for
the offence and is in addition liable to the payment of
compensation for the damage resulting from the breach to
the satisfaction of the Court.

(4) A person shall not be convicted of an offence under
subsection (3) if the person proves that

(a) the person exercised due diligence to secure
compliance with the provisions of this Act; and

(b) the offence was committed without the
knowledge, consent or connivance of that
person.

(5) Where an offence is committed under paragraph
(a) or (c) of subsection (1), the court may order the forfeiture
of the equipment, installation or facility used in the
commission of the offence to the State.”.

Section 54A inserted
3. The principal enactment is amended by the insertion after section

54, of

“Administrative penalties
54A (1) A person who

(a) contravenes any of the conditions of a licence
granted by the Commission under this Act
is liable to pay to the Commission an
administrative penalty often thousand penalty
units in addition to any sanction that the Board
may take under section 19 of the Act;

4

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

(b) fails to comply with a standard of performance
prescribed by the Commission in furtherance
of section 27 is liable to pay to the Commis­
sion an administrative penalty of two thousand
penalty units; or

(c) contravenes the prescribed technical and
operational rules of practice for electricity or
natural gas contrary to section 28 is liable to
pay to the Commission an administrative
penalty of two thousand penalty units.

(2) The Commission may, to ensure compliance, impose
administrative penalties under the Regulations.

(3) Where a person fails to pay an administrative penalty
imposed under subsection (1) or (2) within thirty days, the
Commission shall recover the amount through civil
action.”.

Section 56 of Act 541 amended
4. The principal enactment is amended in section 56 by

(a) the substitution for subsection (1), of

“(1) The Minister, on the advice of the Board may,
by legislative instrument, make Regulations

(a) in respect of electricity and natural gas;

(i) on the conservation of electricity and
natural gas;

5

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

(ii) for the expansion, planning, safety
criteria, reliability and cost
effectiveness of the interconnected
transmission systems;

(iii) on the minimum standards and
procedures for the construction,
operation and maintenance of
facilities and installations;

(iv) for the protection of mains, pipes,
electrical or natural gas installations
and services;

(v) for the protection of life and property
and general safety of the public in
respect of natural gas and electricity
services;

(vi) for the operation of public utilities
which supply electricity;

(vii) for the operation of public utilities
which supply natural gas; and

(viii) for the importation, assembly,
manufacture, sale, installation,
operation and maintenance of
equipment or accessories for the
transmission, wholesale supply,
distribution or sale of electricity or
natural gas; and

6

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

(b) generally,

(i) prescribing fire precautions and any
other safety measures to be observed;

(ii) on the minimum reserve margins to
satisfy demand;

(iii) on the unlawful connection to an
equipment, an installation or a facility
for the supply, transmission,
distribution or sale of electricity or
natural gas; and

(iv) for the implementation of this Act.”;
and

(c) the repeal of subsection (2).

Section 57 of Act 541 amended
5. The principal enactment is amended in section 57 by

(a) the insertion after the definition of “distribution
company”, of

“equipment or accessories” include materials,
instruments, fittings, devices, appliances, apparatus,
fixtures, or parts of materials, instruments, fittings,
devices, appliances, apparatus, fixtures and the like,
that are used as a part of, or in connection with, an
electrical or natural gas installation for the purpose
of wholesale supply, transmission or distribution
and sale of electricity or natural gas;”; and

7

Energy Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2023

(b) the insertion after the definition of “Transmission
Utility”, of

“unlawful connection” means

(a) an illegal or unapproved means of
connecting any equipment or device to an
electricity or natural gas source of a public
utility; or

(b) the unapproved alteration of the electricity
or natural gas installation or facility of a
public utility;”.
